{"id":"ae57a2e7-c20e-40c7-b3b8-62d191075762","audio_id":"631e1a7d-fad0-499e-82c7-7fe55632bac7","status":"complete","created_at":"2026-11-23T00:28:04Z","answer":"The solo female voice sounds light, friendly and generally intelligible; “butterfly” and “flower” are clearly repeated, with no obvious pronunciation error or missing target word in the transcribed singing. The recurring hook is tuneful and easy to recognize: a mostly stepwise, gently rising-and-falling contour over four short, rhyming lines, repeated several times. The backing has a steady, bouncy 4/4 feel at about 128 BPM. There is some space between lines, but the delivery is fairly continuous rather than built around clear child echo pauses; several later verse lines stretch across a longer phrase, so the refrain is the easiest part to copy. I hear no prominent rushed or monotonous section and no obvious distracting audio artifact. The first vocal begins at about 0:02. The final lyric is not fully completed in the audible/aligned vocal: it reaches “We will play another” and does not clearly deliver “hour,” so the ending does not finish the lyric cleanly, despite the instrumental outro resolving. Instrumental-only gaps over two seconds are about 0:09.9–0:13.8, 0:36.2–0:39.4, 0:69.9–0:73.4, and after the final vocal at about 0:84.2 to the track end (1:34.8). One line in the hook is “Butterfly, flutter by”; the target nouns themselves remain clear. Overall, the gentle tone and repetition suit ages 2–4, but the unfinished closing lyric and limited echo space are notable teaching concerns.
